samples.summary: Share-link routes are not excluded from the durable path: the nested provider persists share-link content locally and re-authenticates the attach with the viewer's personal Yorkie token instead of the share token
samples.evidence: The design states share links are "excluded structurally" because `shared-document.tsx` mounts its own `YorkieProvider`. It does — but it mounts it ABOVE `CollabDocumentProvider` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:971-1042 renders `<YorkieProvider authTokenInjector={token ? () => fetchYorkieShareToken(token) : undefined}>` wrapping `<CollabDocumentProvider docKey={`doc-…`|`slides-…`|`note-…`|`board-…`|`sheet-…`} …>`). The new code in `CollabDocumentProvider` nests a `DurableYorkieProvider` INSIDE that, and `useDurableDocument` excludes only `docKey.startsWith('pdf-')` (packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.ts:31-33) — there is no share-route term. Attack/impact chain: a signed-in user opens a share link to a doc/slides/note/board/sheet; `useQuery(['me'], fetchMe)` resolves, `eligible` is true, the tab wins the election, and `CollabDocumentProvider` renders `<DurableYorkieProvider … authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken} …>` (collab-document-provider.tsx:184-197) with `WafflebaseDocStore` attached (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:76-96). Two security consequences: (a) the shared document's full content is written to that machine's IndexedDB and survives revocation/expiry of the share link — the design calls this exclusion a deliberate privacy decision ("the local copy then outlives the share link's revocation"); (b) the attach is re-credentialed with `fetchYorkieToken` (the account session token, api/auth.ts:238) rather than `fetchYorkieShareToken` (api/auth.ts:254, whose webhook "validates the wrapped share token (existence, expiry, role)"), so the share link's role and expiry stop governing that connection. Currently latent only because `supportsClientKey()` reads the `@yorkie-js/react` pin (0.7.22) and the gate opens at 0.7.23 — the task doc records that bumping the dependency is the entire switch, so this ships enabled on the next bump with no further review.

samples.summary: Anonymous share-link visitors are force-logged-out and redirected to /login by the new unconditional `fetchMe` query, which is not behind the version gate
samples.evidence: `CollabDocumentProvider` now unconditionally calls `useQuery({ queryKey: ['me'], queryFn: fetchMe, retry: false })`. `fetchMe` uses `fetchWithAuth` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:116-130), and `fetchWithAuth` on a 401 it cannot refresh calls `logout({redirect:false,…})` and then `redirectTo('/login')`, which sets `window.location.href` (api/auth.ts:213-228, 53-62). `/shared/:token` is a public route (packages/frontend/src/App.tsx:119) and renders `CollabDocumentProvider` for doc/slides/note/board/sheet (shared-document.tsx:979-1042). An unauthenticated visitor therefore hits `/auth/me` → 401 → refresh fails → `logout()` + hard redirect to `/login`, so anonymous share-link access to those five types is denied entirely. The share route deliberately uses `fetchMeOptional` (queryKey `['me','optional']`, shared-document.tsx:900-904) precisely because it returns null instead of redirecting; the new query bypasses that. Unlike the durable path this is NOT gated by `supportsClientKey()` — the query runs before any eligibility check — so it is reachable on the current 0.7.22 pin.

samples.summary: No logout or access-revocation cleanup is wired, so document content this feature writes to disk outlives sign-out and outlives losing access to the document
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:795) and `purge` (line 717) exist but have no production caller: grepping `dropAllForUser|collectStale|purge(` across packages/frontend/src returns only the store, its tests, and `offline-erase.ts` (itself uncalled). `nav-user.tsx:40-42` logs out via `logout()` from `@/api/auth` with no offline erase, and `api/auth.ts`'s `logout` touches no IndexedDB. The design's cleanup table lists "Logout → drop every entry for that user" and "Document deleted, or workspace access lost → drop that entry" as required triggers, and `offline-erase.ts:66-70` even reasons on the assumption that "logout's own cleanup either ran" — it never runs. On a shared/borrowed machine (the exact threat model the opt-in is justified by) a signed-out user's document text, and the archives holding whole documents, remain readable in IndexedDB for up to 30 days, and content whose read authority was revoked is never purged. Latent while the version gate is closed, but it is the state the branch ships in.

samples.summary: `load()` does not verify `header.userId === this.userId` although the record carries it and `loadArchive()` performs exactly that check
samples.evidence: `loadArchive` refuses another user's row (`if (!row || row.userId !== this.userId) return undefined;`, line 758-766) and documents the reason ("an id can be held across a sign-out and the listing is not the only way in"). `load` (line 419-458) applies no such check: it returns any stored snapshot/meta/log for the key given. Cross-account reads are prevented today only by the SDK's key shape embedding `clientKey = wb:{userId}:{docKey}` — which the store's own `HeaderRecord.userId` comment (line 63-69) explicitly says is "the SDK's to change", and which the SDK does not honour at all on the current pin (`supportsClientKey()` false ⇒ a random per-session clientKey). One shared `wafflebase-offline` database serves every account on the device, so the only barrier between accounts on the live-entry path is a key format outside this repo's control. Adding the same `header.userId !== this.userId ⇒ undefined` guard to `load` makes the isolation enforced rather than inherited.

samples.summary: An archive of a header-less (torn-write) entry is attributed to whoever is currently signed in, making another account's bytes listable and loadable by them
samples.evidence: `remove()` builds the archive with `userId: header?.userId ?? this.userId` (line 691). If the header row is missing — the torn-write shape the atomicity tests in this change exist to describe — the archived snapshot is stamped with the *current* store's `userId`, and `listArchives`/`loadArchive` scope purely on that stamp (lines 736-766). The snapshot bytes archived in that case belong to whatever was in the snapshot store under that key. Reachability is narrow because the key embeds the owning user's clientKey, so I could not complete a concrete cross-account chain; but the safe direction is to skip the archive (or drop the entry) when the header that carries the identity is absent, rather than substituting the caller's identity onto someone else's bytes.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. shared-document.tsx:971-976 mounts the share-token YorkieProvider ABOVE CollabDocumentProvider (shared-document.tsx:978-1043, docKeys built at :960-969 with doc-/slides-/note-/board-/sheet- prefixes), and collab-document-provider.tsx:189-208 nests its own DurableYorkieProvider inside that with authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken} (the account-session token, api/auth.ts:238) rather than fetchYorkieShareToken (api/auth.ts:254), plus the IndexedDB WafflebaseDocStore (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:76-96). use-durable-document.ts:31-33 excludes only docKey.startsWith("pdf-") — there is no share-route term, and eligibility (:78-79) depends only on supportsClientKey/preference/userId, where userId comes from useQuery(['me'], fetchMe) which resolves for any signed-in share-link visitor. The "excluded structurally" claim in docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:81-91,233-234 and in the component comment (collab-document-provider.tsx:139-140) is therefore false: the inner provider shadows the outer share-token client. The only thing preventing this today is the build-time version pin (package.json:65 = 0.7.22 vs MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23, yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,61-67) plus the off-by-default preference; yorkie-capabilities.ts:59 documents that bumping the dependency is the sole switch, so this is a capability pin, not a security guard, and I will not refute on it. Impact under the security lens is real: share-link content persisted to local disk surviving link revocation/expiry, and an attach re-credentialed with the personal session token so the share link's role and expiry no longer govern the connection.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described — collab-document-provider.tsx:152-156 issues an ungated `useQuery(['me'], fetchMe)` before the `supportsClientKey()`/eligibility gate in use-durable-document.ts:78-79, fetchMe routes through fetchWithAuth which on an unrefreshable 401 calls logout() and hard-redirects to /login (auth.ts:116-130, 213-228, 53-62), and the public /shared/:token route (App.tsx:119) renders CollabDocumentProvider for all five types (shared-document.tsx:979-1042) while its own identity query uses the distinct ["me","optional"] key (shared-document.tsx:900-904). However, the resulting impact is fail-CLOSED: legitimate anonymous share-link visitors are denied access. That is a functional/availability regression owned by the correctness lens, not any category in the security lane. I checked for a real security angle and found none: for anonymous visitors `me` is undefined so `durable` is false and DurableYorkieProvider (which would replace the share-token injector fetchYorkieShareToken at shared-document.tsx:976 with the session token fetchYorkieToken at collab-document-provider.tsx:198) never mounts — no credential substitution or privilege escalation; for authenticated visitors /auth/me returns 200 so an attacker cannot induce the logout; the redirect target is the hardcoded "/login" (auth.ts:226) so there is no open redirect, and no secret or user data is exposed. No missing/weakened permission gate, IDOR, injection, secret exposure, or broken crypto check is involved.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: no production code wires any cleanup of the offline document store on logout or access loss. Repo-wide grep for dropAllForUser|eraseOfflineData|watchForOfflineDisable|purge yields only the store's own internals, offline-erase.ts, tests, and docs — offline-erase.ts is imported solely by its own test (offline-erase.test.ts:4). The only production instantiation of WafflebaseDocStore is durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:78, which uses it only for expectLoss (:127). Both logout call paths — nav-user.tsx:40-41 and the 401 handler at api/auth.ts:221-227 — reach api/auth.ts:80-110, which only POSTs /auth/logout, toasts, and redirects, touching no IndexedDB. No caller of purge() exists outside the store's own archive/eviction paths (:798, :834, :847, :995), so document-deleted / access-lost cleanup is absent too. The repo's own task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:173) records the same gap. I considered refuting on already-guarded via the supportsClientKey version gate (use-durable-document.ts:79, yorkie-capabilities.ts:61-67), but that gate controls whether data is written, not whether written data is erased; a dependency bump alone opens it with cleanup still unwired, so it is not a counterexample. In-lane as sensitive data exposure: document text and full-document archives survive sign-out and survive revocation of read authority on a shared machine.
